Fit multiple Gaussian graphical models via MCMC

Source: R/multiggm_mcmc.R
multiggm_mcmc.Rd

Implements Bayesian inference of multiple Gaussian graphical models following Peterson, Stingo & Vannucci (2015, JASA). Simultaneously estimates K group-specific precision matrices and their conditional independence graphs, borrowing strength across groups through a Markov random field (MRF) prior. Supports both raw data and pre-computed cross-product matrices, with optional parallel multi-chain execution.

Usage

multiggm_mcmc(
  data_list = NULL,
  S_list = NULL,
  n_vec = NULL,
  burnin = 5000,
  nsave = 1000,
  thin = 1,
  nchains = 1,
  parallel = FALSE,
  ncores = max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L),
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gwishart", "ssvs", "ssvs_platform", "mghs"),
  platform_data = NULL,
  hyper = NULL,
  engine = c("cpp", "R"),
  ...
)

Arguments

data_list

Optional list of K data matrices (each n_k x p). If provided, S_list and n_vec are computed automatically. Column-centers data internally. Exactly one of data_list or S_list must be given.

S_list

Optional list of K cross-product matrices (each p x p), where S_list[[k]] = t(X_k) %*% X_k after column-centering.

n_vec

Integer vector of length K with sample sizes. Required when S_list is provided; ignored when data_list is provided.

burnin

Integer number of burn-in iterations (discarded). Default 5000.

nsave

Integer number of posterior draws to save per chain (after burn-in and thinning). Default 1000.

thin

Integer thinning interval; every thin-th post-burn-in iteration is saved. Default 1 (no thinning).

nchains

Integer number of independent MCMC chains. Default 1.

parallel

Logical; if TRUE, run chains in parallel using parallel. Default FALSE.

ncores

Integer number of cores/workers when parallel = TRUE. Default is one less than the number of detected cores.

seed

Optional integer random seed. If provided, chain i uses seed seed + 1000 * (i - 1) for reproducibility.

method

Character; "gwishart" (default) uses the G-Wishart prior with the Wang-Li exchange algorithm (Peterson et al. 2015). "ssvs" uses a spike-and-slab normal prior on precision elements with column-wise Gibbs sampling (Shaddox et al. 2018), which scales to larger dimensions. "ssvs_platform" extends the SSVS approach to jointly model multiple data platforms (Shaddox et al. 2020, Biostatistics) with a hierarchical MRF coupling group similarity across platforms. Requires platform_data. "mghs" uses the multiple graphical horseshoe (Busatto & Stingo 2025): continuous horseshoe shrinkage on each precision matrix, with each edge's local scales correlated across groups. It has no edge-inclusion indicators; see Details.

platform_data

For method = "ssvs_platform" only. A list of S elements (one per platform), each a list with components data_list or S_list and n_vec. Each platform may have different dimensions p_s, but must have the same number of groups K.

hyper

Optional named list of hyperparameters. See Details.

engine

Character; "cpp" (default) uses the high-performance C++ MCMC engine. "R" uses the pure R fallback (slower, mainly for debugging). Only applies when method = "gwishart".

...

Additional arguments forwarded to the single-chain engine. For method = "gwishart", "ssvs" and "mghs": save_draws (default TRUE; FALSE keeps only the running summaries, see "Edge probabilities and memory") and diff_deltas (the thresholds c for the running probabilities \(P(|x| > c)\), \(P(|D| > c)\) and the union rule, default c(0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.10)), mcse_batches (number of batches for the Monte Carlo SEs of edge probabilities, default 20; 0 turns them off), waic (TRUE keeps the per-observation sums for compute_waic(); needs data_list) and prior_only (TRUE ignores the data and samples the prior, for edge_bayes_factors(); not for mGHS). For method = "mghs" also max_attempts (restarts allowed when the chain gets stuck, default 3).

Value

For a single chain (nchains = 1), an object of class "multiggm_fit" with the following components:

K

Integer; number of groups.

p

Integer; number of variables (nodes).

C_save

Numeric array [p, p, K, nsave]; posterior draws of the precision matrices \(\Omega_k\). C_save[,,k,s] is the precision matrix for group k at saved iteration s.

Sig_save

Numeric array [p, p, K, nsave]; posterior draws of the covariance matrices \(\Sigma_k = \Omega_k^{-1}\). Sig_save[,,k,s] is the covariance matrix for group k at saved iteration s.

adj_save

Integer array [p, p, K, nsave]; posterior draws of the adjacency matrices \(G_k\). adj_save[i,j,k,s] is 1 if edge (i,j) is included in group k at iteration s, 0 otherwise.

Theta_save

Numeric array [K, K, nsave]; posterior draws of the graph similarity parameters \(\theta_{km}\). Theta_save[k,m,s] measures similarity between graphs k and m at iteration s. Values > 0 indicate the model borrows strength between those groups.

nu_save

Numeric array [p, p, nsave]; posterior draws of the edge-specific log-odds parameters \(\nu_{ij}\). nu_save[i,j,s] controls the baseline edge inclusion probability for edge (i,j) across all groups at iteration s.

ar_gamma

Numeric matrix [K, K]; acceptance rates for the between-model (spike-slab toggle) moves on \(\theta_{km}\). Upper triangle only.

ar_theta

Numeric matrix [K, K]; acceptance rates for the within-model (slab-to-slab) moves on \(\theta_{km}\). Upper triangle only. Only meaningful when \(\theta_{km} > 0\).

ar_nu

Numeric matrix [p, p]; acceptance rates for the \(\nu_{ij}\) MH updates. Upper triangle only.

hyper

Named list of the hyperparameters used.

call

The matched function call.

For multiple chains (nchains > 1), an object of class "multiggm_fit_list" with components:

chains

List of nchains multiggm_fit objects.

call

The matched function call.

K

Integer; number of groups.

nchains

Integer; number of chains.

Details

Method selection: method = "gwishart" uses the G-Wishart prior on precision matrices with the Wang-Li (2012) exchange algorithm. Accurate but computationally expensive for \(p > 30\). method = "ssvs" replaces this with a spike-and-slab normal prior, enabling column-wise Gibbs sampling that scales to \(p > 100\). Both methods use the same MRF prior for borrowing strength across groups.

The hyper list may contain any of the following:

Common hyperparameters (both methods):

a, b

Beta(a, b) prior on \(q_{ij} = \text{logit}^{-1}(\nu_{ij})\). Default a = 1, b = 4, giving prior edge probability \(\approx 0.20\).

alpha, beta

Gamma(shape = alpha, rate = beta) slab prior on \(\theta_{km}\). NOTE: beta is a RATE parameter. Default alpha = 2, beta = 5, giving mean = 0.4.

w

Bernoulli prior probability that \(\gamma_{km} = 1\) (graph similarity active). Default 0.9 (strong prior belief that groups are related).

alpha_prop, beta_prop

Gamma(shape = alpha_prop, rate = beta_prop) proposal for \(\theta_{km}\), a RATE like beta (all samplers). Default alpha_prop = 2, beta_prop = 5 for G-Wishart; alpha_prop = 1, beta_prop = 1 for SSVS.

G-Wishart-specific hyperparameters (method = "gwishart"):

b_prior

G-Wishart degrees of freedom (default 3).

D_prior

G-Wishart scale matrix, p x p (default diag(p)).

SSVS-specific hyperparameters (method = "ssvs" or "ssvs_platform"):

v0

Spike variance for off-diagonal precision elements (default 0.02^2 = 0.0004).

v1

Slab variance for off-diagonal precision elements (default 50^2 * v0 = 1.0).

lambda

Exponential rate hyperparameter for diagonal elements (default 1).

mGHS hyperparameters (method = "mghs"):

t_mean, t_var

Mean and variance of the Beta prior on the cut-model threshold. Default 0.6 and 0.05, the values used by the authors' simulation scripts. The cut model does not feed back into the precision matrices.

R_eta

Shape \(\eta\) of an LKJ prior on the correlation of edge scales across groups, \(\pi(R) \propto |R|^{\eta - 1}\). Default 1, the paper's uniform prior (the sampler is then unchanged). With few observations per group, the posterior of \(R\) under the uniform prior piles up at \(\pm 1\), because the per-group local scales can align the scaled edges of the groups and null edges carry no sign information; the chain then fails with "global-scale parameter above 1e6" and an error message naming R_eta. In that case use \(\eta > 1\): on a TCGA example (K = 2, n = 100, p = 28) \(\eta = 5\) and \(\eta = 10\) ran without failure where \(\eta \le 3\) failed, and partial correlations and differential edge probabilities changed little between them, while the posterior of \(R\) itself moved with \(\eta\). Treat \(R\) as a nuisance parameter in that regime. For K = 2, \(R_{12}\) has a Beta(\(\eta\), \(\eta\)) distribution stretched to (-1, 1).

mGHS sampler (method = "mghs"): the horseshoe prior is continuous, so the sampler has no edge indicators: adj_save and Sig_save are NULL, and pip_edges(), pip_diff_edge(), edge_counts(), plot(type = "pip") and plot_recovery() stop with an error. Select differential edges with select_diff_edges() (rule = "magnitude"). Do not call differences by whether a credible interval excludes zero: under a continuous prior that rule is badly anti-conservative (see diff_summary()). The fit also contains R_save ([K, K, nsave], correlation of edge scales across groups), tau_save ([K, nsave], global shrinkage), C_mean and pcor_mean (posterior means over every post-burn-in iteration), diff_acc (running sums of group differences), cut_z_mean and ta_save (the authors' cut-model edge selection, kept for reference only) and attempts. Storage is \(8 p^2 K\) nsave bytes per chain (160 MB at p = 100, K = 2, nsave = 1000); use thin to reduce nsave, or save_draws = FALSE, in which case diff_summary(), coef() and fitted() use the running summaries and draw-based functions stop with an error. A chain whose shrinkage parameters become non-finite is restarted from scratch, up to max_attempts times.

Edge probabilities and memory. Every sampler except "ssvs_platform" keeps running sums over every post-burn-in iteration (edge_acc) from which edge_probs(), select_edges() and select_diff_edges() compute per-group and per-pair posterior edge probabilities, and C_mean / pcor_mean (posterior means). They do not draw random numbers, so a chain is the same with or without them. Their size grows with the number of edges \(p(p-1)/2\), the number of group pairs and the number of thresholds in diff_deltas: with K = 2 and the default 5 thresholds, about 5 MB at p = 100 and 30 MB at p = 250, half of which are the batch counts for Monte Carlo SEs (mcse_batches = 0 drops them). Saved draws take \(8 p^2 K\) nsave bytes for the precision matrices alone (160 MB at p = 100, K = 2, nsave = 1000); G-Wishart and SSVS also save covariance, edge-indicator and \(\nu\) draws of similar size. With save_draws = FALSE only the running sums and the small traces are kept; thresholds c must then come from diff_deltas, so choose a fine grid if you want to pick c after fitting.

Diagnostics. Every sampler except "ssvs_platform" also keeps, without drawing random numbers:

  • trace: per post-burn-in iteration, the number of edges per group, the number of differential edges per pair of groups (structural, \(|D| > c\) and union, for each c) and the log-likelihood of each group, used by mcmc_diagnostics(), plot_trace() and diff_count_posterior();

  • batch counts in edge_acc$batch for the Monte Carlo SE of every edge probability (mcse_* columns of edge_probs()), which roughly double the size of edge_acc;

  • node-level sums in edge_acc$node for node_diff_summary();

  • with waic = TRUE, waic_acc for compute_waic(): \(3 n_k\) numbers per group, at a cost of \(O(n_k p^2)\) per iteration.

The log-likelihood needs one Cholesky factorization per group and iteration (\(O(p^3)\)), small next to a sampler sweep.

Platform-level hyperparameters (method = "ssvs_platform" only):

eta, kappa

Gamma(shape = eta, scale = kappa) slab prior on platform similarity \(\Phi_{st}\). Default eta = 4, kappa = 5.

eta_prop, kappa_prop

Gamma(shape = eta_prop, scale = kappa_prop) proposal for \(\Phi_{st}\), a SCALE like kappa. Default eta_prop = 1, kappa_prop = 1.

d, f

Beta(d, f) prior on platform-level edge log-odds \(w_{km}\). Default d = 1, f = 19.

d_prop, f_prop

Beta proposal for \(w_{km}\). Default d_prop = 2, f_prop = 4.

u_prior

Bernoulli prior probability \(P(\zeta_{st} = 1)\). Default 0.1.

References

Peterson, C.B., Stingo, F.C. & Vannucci, M. (2015). Bayesian inference of multiple Gaussian graphical models. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 110(509), 159-174.

Shaddox, E., Stingo, F.C., Peterson, C.B., et al. (2018). A Bayesian approach for learning gene networks underlying disease severity in COPD. Statistics in Biosciences, 10(1), 59-85.

Shaddox, E., Peterson, C.B., Stingo, F.C., et al. (2020). Bayesian inference of networks across multiple sample groups and data types. Biostatistics, 21(3), 561-576.

Busatto, C. & Stingo, F.C. (2025). Inference of multiple high-dimensional networks with the Graphical Horseshoe prior. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 1-12. doi:10.1080/10618600.2024.2435480

Busatto, C. & Stingo, F.C. (2025). The multiple graphical horseshoe: an application to breast cancer data. In SIS 2025, 435-440. Springer. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-96736-8_72

See also

pip_edges(), posterior_precision(), posterior_pcor(), summary.multiggm_fit(), coef.multiggm_fit(), fitted.multiggm_fit()

Examples

# Short runs to keep the example fast; real analyses need far more
# iterations (see mcmc_diagnostics()).
sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 8, n = 100, seed = 42)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, burnin = 200, nsave = 100)
summary(fit)
#> multiGGM MCMC Summary
#> =====================
#> Groups (K): 2   |  Nodes (p): 8   |  Posterior draws: 100 
#> 
#> Acceptance rates:
#>   gamma (edge toggle): 3.0% 
#>   theta (within-model): 44.3% 
#>   nu (edge log-odds): 56.4% 
#> 
#> Selected edges (PIP >= 0.5 ):
#>   Group 1 : 8 edges
#>   Group 2 : 9 edges
#> 
#> Graph similarity (theta):
#>   theta[1,2]: mean = 0.574, P(nonzero) = 99.0%
#> 

# Multiple chains (parallel on Unix/macOS, sequential on Windows)
fit_mc <- multiggm_mcmc(
  data_list = sim$data_list, burnin = 200, nsave = 100,
  nchains = 2, parallel = TRUE, ncores = 2, seed = 42
)
fit_mc                          # prints chain count and K
#> <multiggm_fit_list>
#>   Chains: 2 
#>   K groups: 2 
summary(fit_mc$chains[[1]])     # summarize first chain
#> multiGGM MCMC Summary
#> =====================
#> Groups (K): 2   |  Nodes (p): 8   |  Posterior draws: 100
